sections.title: Sound, made visible
paragraphs: The DSP lab turns audio playback into an interactive signal display. Two analog-style VU meters show the left and right channels, while a VFD-style spectrum analyzer reveals the frequencies in the output.
Choose one of the website's default tracks or load a mono or stereo WAV from your device. Press Play to hear the track and see the analysis in real time.

sections.title: Inside the signal path
bullets: The Web Audio API handles decoding, playback, channel separation, and analysis.
Channel RMS levels drive the VU needles. An adjustable RC time constant controls their exponential response.
An 8192-point FFT feeds a logarithmic frequency display drawn on a high-resolution canvas.
The default music library reads the WAV files bundled in the website's public/music folder.

sections.title: A story told through a terminal
paragraphs: Cate's Terminal presents the Leo & Cate story as a fictional computer startup sequence, from hardware checks and memory mapping to CateOS and the security system notice.
Visitors can type at the prompt. Every submitted command receives an in-world error: Leo's connection has reserved the TTY. The terminal also carries his message that the story is still in progress.

sections.title: How it is built
bullets: The BIOS text and story metadata live in Markdown, keeping the writing separate from the interface.
A React command prompt keeps a local command history and returns scripted responses.
Green terminal output and a red security notice create the console theme.
A labelled input, keyboard submission, and an accessible response log support interaction.
